LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about chores and fun activities.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#7 After-School Activities Song
•	 TR#10 Puppy Song

(P.1.2)

Chores playing cards (P.1.5)

(P.S1)

BEFORE CLASS
Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed 
at least half of the recommended activities up to this point.

This worksheet shows images of different fun activities and 
chores. The Ss must follow your instructions and write the 
correct number in the circle beside each picture. 
If needed, review the vocabulary on the worksheet first. Then 
explain the task to the Ss and dictate three phrases
If you see they have understood the task, let a S take on 
the teacher role and call out what number to write and where.
EXAMPLE INSTRUCTIONS:
Playing video games is number 61.
Riding a bike is number 78.
Taking out the rubbish is number 82.
Taking Billy for a walk is number 54.
Reading a book is number 89.
Drawing a picture is number 93.
Watching TV is number 97.
To review, ask Ss, “What is number 82?” and they should 
respond, “Number 82 is taking out rubbish.”

Story 1: The Puppy
> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 1, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 5 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic. 
The point of this activity is to review chores in a fun way using 
the sticker pages. Ss have to stick the stickers and answer the 
questions by looking at the stickers with Billy on them. Model 
the task with your Ss by looking for the stickers, sticking them, 
and answering the questions.

Have Ss open p.25 (sticker section) and say, “Let’s imagine 
we are Pam and Paul! Why do we have to take care of Billy? 
Let’s find out!”. Point to square number 71 and ask, “What 
number is this?”, to which Ss should respond, “It’s number 
71!”. Say, “Can you find number 71 on the sheet? What is it?”, 
and elicit, “Here it is! It’s feeding Billy”. Have Ss place the 
sticker and ask them, “Why do Pam and Paul have to feed 
Billy?”, eliciting the response: “We have to feed Billy because 
he’s hungry!”. You can ask them to point at the correct bubble 
(Billy thinking about food) to ensure comprehension.
Stick as many stickers as time allows, but don’t worry if you 
can’t finish the whole page. Tell the Ss that they can continue 
at home.
KEY (From left to right, top to bottom)
Sticker 71: Pam, Paul, why do you have to feed Billy? 
We have to feed Billy because he’s hungry. (point to Billy 
thinking about food)
Sticker 72: Pam, Paul, why do you have to give Billy some 
water? We have to give Billy some water because he’s 
thirsty. (point to Billy thinking about water)
Sticker 73: Pam, Paul, why do you have to pick up Billy’s 
poo? We have to pick up Billy’s poo because there’s dog 
poo all over the garden. (Billy thinking about poo)
Sticker 74: Pam, Paul, why do you have to wash Billy? 
We have to wash Billy because he’s dirty. (Billy thinking 
about being dirty)
6.– ACTIVITY 2: CAN’T/MUST (8’)
P.1.2
P.1.2
P.1.2
> How to Play
Prepare six sets of Playing cards (P.1.2) and place them on 
the table face down in this order:
•	 Character cards (x10: 2 cards per character except 
Grandpa and Grandma)
•	 Red “X” for “can’t” (x10)
•	 Green “V” for “must” (x10)
•	 Fun Activity cards (x10)
•	 Chores cards (x11)

> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
Introduce the activity by saying “Pam, Paul and their family 
want to do their favourite activities, but they can’t! They must 
do their chores first! Look.”. Turn over a card from each pile and 
form the target structure, encouraging the Ss to repeat after you. 
Emphasise “can’t”, “must” and “he/she” so they understand 
the symbols. Say, for example: “Pam can’t listen to music now, 
she must take out the rubbish first.”
> Main Activity
The Ss should take one card from each of the piles mentioned 
above, in the established order, and say, for example, “Grandpa 
can’t play video games, he must take out the rubbish first.”. 
They can either say the phrase as they turn each card or after 
they have turned all five. When a S finishes making the phrase, 
you can keep their pile of cards.
Each S should make at least one phrase. If you have time, 
you can start again and make new phrases.
NOTE: you can have the Ss make phrases in pairs and reward 
correct phrases with points. You can keep track of them by 
marking the cards with a board marker, or by drawing stars 
next to their name on the board.
> Follow-Up
Once each S has created a phrase, turn over one or two new 
sets of cards and ask them comprehension questions following 
this model:
•	 “What must Grandpa do?”: encourage the Ss to practise 
using he/she when answering, “He must make the 
bed.” by pointing at the “He/she” cards. 
•	 “Can Grandpa play video games?”: encourage the Ss 
to answer “No, he can’t! He must make the bed first.”

> How to Play
This is based on the traditional card game Go Fish. The point 
of the game is to find pairs of matching cards by asking the 
other players for them. In this case, Ss must match the day of 
the week and the chore that Pam and Paul had to do that day.
> Warm-Up
Bring a SB with you and use p.4 (Story Comprehension) as a 
visual aid. Preferably, the worksheet would have been completed 
previously. 
Show the Monday card (P.1.5) and ask the Ss “What must 
Pam and Paul do on Monday?”. Ss must answer, “On Monday, 
Pam and Paul must wash Billy.”. Review the whole week in 
the same manner:
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Monday?” 	
 
“On Monday, Pam and Paul must wash Billy.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Tuesday?” 	
 
“On Tuesday, Pam and Paul must feed Billy.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Wednesday?”  
“On Wednesday, Pam and Paul must take Billy for 
a walk.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Thursday?” 	  
“On Thursday, Pam and Paul must pick up Billy’s poo.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Friday?” 	
 
“On Friday, Pam and Paul must give Billy some water.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Saturday?” 	  
“On Saturday, Pam and Paul must brush Billy.” 
•	 “What happens on Sunday?” 	
 
“On Sunday, Billy is with Grandma.” 
> Main Activity
To play, you should first shuffle the cards (P.1.5) while saying, 
“Mix, mix, mix” and have the Ss say, “Stop!” 
Then deal three cards to each S and put the rest of the cards 
in a pile face down on the table. Explain to the Ss that they 
must find pairs. Ss must ask another S for a card and try to 
match it with one of the cards in their hand. They can either 
ask for the day of the week or the chore: 
•	 “Jane, have you got Friday?”
•	 “Jane, have you got ‘brush Billy’?”
Jane should either:
•	 Say “Yes, I have, here you are!” and hand it over to 
the S who asked for it. 
•	 Say “No, I haven’t. Take a card!” and the S who asked 
must pick up a card from the deck.

When a S finds a pair, they must then place the pair face 
up on the table and say, “I’ve got a pair!”. After that, it is the 
next Ss’ turn.
The game continues with the Ss taking turns asking for the 
card they need from the other players. If a player gets all their 
cards stolen, they have to draw a card from the pile on their turn. 
The game is over when there are no cards left on the deck in 
the middle, or when time is up. At this point, ask the Ss one by 
one, “How many pairs have you got?” and the S must answer, 
“I’ve got five pairs.” The S with the most pairs is the winner.
NOTE: if you have a small group, you might want to halve 
the deck to speed up the activity. 
> Follow-Up
Take the winner’s pairs and ask the group: “What pairs has 
Jane got?”. Point to the cards and elicit from the whole group: 
“On Tuesday, Pam and Paul must feed Billy. On Monday...” 
8.– ACTIVITY 6: NUMBERS (VERSION 3) (6’) 
P.E.M.3
55
> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
If you feel like your group needs it, quickly review the numbers 
by using the Number cards (P.E.M.3.) without the jokers. Turn 
over one card at a time and, as a group, say, “It’s number 55!” 
> Main Activity
This is a relay game. Divide the class into two teams. Get 
each team to form a line in front of the whiteboard. Give each 
team a whiteboard marker, draw a card from the deck (P.E.M.3.) 
and call out the number. One S from each team must run to 
the board and write the number. Keep saying numbers until 
every S has written one. Then check these numbers using the 
cards. The team with the most correct numbers written on 
the board wins.

NOTE: it might be helpful to divide the board into two (Team 1, 
Team 2) and to make each team line up in front of their section.

10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
ACTIVITY 4: CHARADES (VERSION 2)
P.1.2
Play the game in the Pictionary style, using the whiteboard. 
A S must take a Fun Activity card (P.1.2.), ask the group “What 
am I doing?”, and draw the action on the board. The rest of the

Ss try to guess by asking, “Are you watching TV?” to which the 
S must reply, “Yes, I am.” or “No, I’m not.”. To ensure everyone 
gets a turn, set a timer for each round (30 seconds should be 
enough). 
ACTIVITY 7: SWITCH!
> How to Play
This is a group hand clapping game to practise counting. To 
play, you must have all the Ss sitting in a circle, either on the 
floor or at the table.
> Main Activity
If you do the activity sitting on chairs, the Ss should sit with 
their palms facing up on the table. If you do it on the floor, the 
Ss place their palms on their legs.
The Ss must place their right hand on top of the hand of the 
S sitting to their right, and their left hand underneath the hand 
of the person on their left. This way when they begin to clap, 
they will use their right hand to clap the hand of the person 
to their left and the clapping will continue around the circle.
Start counting from number 50 until you get to 99. If someone 
makes a mistake, the Ss switch the position of their hands (right 
hand below, left hand on top). If this is too difficult, simply move 
on with the game without switching hand positions.
NOTE: if time allows, increase the difficulty by starting from 
number one or counting backwards.
